title: Gate 3 closes on machine evidence: release.decide auto-approves a gap-free criterion-bound dossier under a recorded opt-in
description:
SPIDR child C of parent task-d56a0cc5f6ae4dc88da5233a9702d9e6 ("One approval, then unattended"), split 2026-09-09 by architect-fa84777a. Sibling of child A (task-a47301ee3aa64866ba109d4c0283526f, the mapping + carried opt-ins leaf) and child B (Gate 2 / preview.decide). This row is Gate 3 ONLY.

DEPENDS ON TWO ROWS, both declared in dependsOn and both currently unlanded:
- task-a47301ee3aa64866ba109d4c0283526f supplies the AdvisoryRiskClass -> PolicyRiskTier mapping and makes the live dispatch carry auto-approval opt-ins instead of `autoApprovalOptIns: []`. Without it there is no opt-in for this gate to act under.
- task-b8ec9a638f6540c28798c29f23fd5ada ("Release evidence is bound to criterion receipts at the released SHA") supplies the criterion-bound dossier. MEASURED 2026-09-09: that row is status PLANNING with commits 0 - the criterion-bound dossier DOES NOT EXIST at HEAD yet. Auto-releasing on today's dossier would auto-release on evidence weaker than goal closure demands, which is exactly the defect the 2026-09-09 external review found. Do NOT plan against a dossier shape until that row lands; read its verification and completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings rather than re-measuring HEAD.

OWNER DIRECTION driving the parent (2026-09-09): "we dont want moe-next to be stuck all the time for user approval we can approve the plan at the start but thats it". One human gate at plan/contract time; the rest unattended, with a human ABLE to intervene but not REQUIRED.

MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-09 by architect-fa84777a; re-measure before planning:
- `git grep -ln "evaluatePolicy|PolicyRiskTier|autoApprovalOptIns" -- apps/daemon/src/release/**` returns NOTHING. The release gate does not consult the policy engine at all today. This row BUILDS that consumption path; it is not flipping on a dark switch. The parent's description called the engine "dark", which is true of the two seams it names but understates this: there is no policy call at either gate.
- The decision function this row must call, and must NOT reimplement, is packages/core/src/policy/policy-evaluation.ts assessTier at :150-166. R2/R3 return REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL with code HUMAN_ONLY_TIER (:155-158). A tier with no matching opt-in returns REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL with code AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN (:165). An opt-in matches only when `entry.action === action && tierRank(entry.tier) >= tierRank(tier)`.
- policy-composition.ts foldSlices at :132-170 returns `optIns: last.autoApprovalOptIns` - the LAST slice in the chain wins. An opt-in that is not in the final slice is not in effect.
- apps/daemon/src/release/ holds release-decide-contracts.ts, release-decide-command.ts, release-decide-service.ts, release-decide-wiring.test.ts, release-dossier-contracts.ts, release-dossier-ledger.ts and their tests. RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND is defined in release-decide-contracts.ts and consumed at daemon-command-async-entries.ts:11,59,193,353-356.
- release.decide is in OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:405) and MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS is DERIVED from that set, so a roster edit opens TWO fences in one line. Landed rows task-54b74b8041c64 and task-20b7d6bba60f4 established that fence deliberately.

WHO SUBMITS THE AUTOMATIC DECISION. Do NOT widen the MCP allowlist and do NOT let an agent seat decide a gate. The automatic decision is taken SERVER-SIDE inside the daemon under the operator principal acting on a recorded opt-in, never as a wire command from a seat. Governor ruling of 2026-09-06 (quoted on task-136cbab2, comment-b0d0a809c1a7445e91f03f83ea69329d) is binding: do NOT remove a kind from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS; if you find yourself editing a roster you have left the approved scope, stop and report. The precedent for a typed narrow arm is the SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER handling in the registry.

A MANUAL REJECT WINS. If a human has already recorded a REJECT for the release, the automatic path must not overturn it, and the refusal must carry a stable code asserted WITH its layer. Prefer an EXISTING code from the release refusal vocabulary over minting a new one; POLICY_REASON_CODES in packages/core is a closed frozen list and this row does not own it.

OUT OF SCOPE, owned by siblings: the risk-class mapping and the carried opt-ins (row A); anything under apps/daemon/src/preview/ (row B); the end-to-end unattended journey arm (the parent). Do not widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS.
definitionOfDone: release.decide consults the policy engine: a production module under apps/daemon/src/release/ calls evaluatePolicy from the @moe/core bare specifier and does NOT reimplement tier or opt-in logic; `git grep -n 'evaluatePolicy' -- apps/daemon/src/release/` returns at least one non-test hit, quoted in the completion record.

An arm proves the AUTOMATIC APPROVE path: a gap-free criterion-bound dossier at the released SHA, under a recorded R0 or R1 opt-in whose action equals RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND, is released with NO human decision, and the persisted decision record NAMES the opt-in it acted under (action and tier), so a reviewer can tell an automatic approval from a human one. Assert the recorded provenance fields, not merely that the outcome was ACCEPTED.

An arm proves a dossier carrying a CRITERION GAP is NOT auto-released even under a valid R0 opt-in, asserting the specific stable gap code AND the layer that refused. The gap code must be read from the prerequisite row's landed dossier vocabulary (task-b8ec9a638f6540c28798c29f23fd5ada), never invented here.

An arm proves R2 and R3 are not auto-released: the gate stays pending for a human and the refusal carries HUMAN_ONLY_TIER from evaluatePolicy, asserted with its layer. A separate arm asserts POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS still deep-equals ['R0','R1'] and that this row modified no file under packages/core/src/policy/.

An arm proves a recorded human REJECT WINS: with a manual REJECT already recorded and a valid R0 opt-in present, the automatic path does not overturn it and refuses with a stable code asserted together with its layer. Verify non-vacuity by mutating the precedence check in the production module and confirming this arm goes RED, with the drill's restore proven by SHA256 equality against an out-of-tree backup whose path carries this task id.

The human-only fence is UNCHANGED: RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND is still in OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS and still in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS, and no agent seat or MCP tool can submit a gate decision. Assert BOTH directions per global rail 9 - enumerate the served set from the dispatch seam, not only from the roster constant - and leave the existing wiring and authorization tests green.

pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXITS 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted and NONZERO, and pnpm typecheck exits 0. If any command kind or payload shape changed, all four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors are re-censused with a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types and pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test is also run and quoted; if nothing changed, state that explicitly with the census command output.

implementationPlan.description: THE LEAF: apps/daemon/src/release/release-auto-approval.ts (NEW, target <=250) plus its tracked one-line `.js` bridge, as every module in release/ has. Two responsibilities, one module. (A) `evaluateReleaseAutoApproval(store, {projectId, goalId, sha, operatorPrincipalId})` calls `evaluatePolicy` from the `@moe/core` BARE specifier — DoD 1 forbids reimplementing tier or opt-in logic. Inputs the daemon convention already uses (approval-record-facts.ts:215-231): tier from `readCriterionGoal(store, projectId, goalId).graph.planningRunRef` -> `readRunPolicyEvaluation(store, {projectId, runId}).evaluation.riskTier` (replay-verified, daemon-computed); ONE fact `{factId: \`release.run_policy_tier:${runId}\`, tier: riskTier, truthClass: "DAEMON_VERIFIED"}`; `action: RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND`; `actor: operatorPrincipalId`; `decisionDigest: "0".repeat(64)` (run-policy-evaluation.ts:168 precedent); `evaluatorVersion: POLICY_EVALUATOR_VERSION`; `scope: [goalId]`; `sliceChain: [<the LAST digest-addressed installed evaluation slice>]` chosen exactly as run-policy-selection-snapshot.ts:92-99 does; `waivers: []`. Absent run-policy row or slice -> yield, fail closed. The opt-in is NAMED for provenance by `slice.autoApprovalOptIns.find(e => e.action === RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND)` — a lookup for naming, never a second decision; ALLOW with no nameable opt-in -> yield (Gate 2's rule). (B) The auto-approval RECORD codec + ledger: store-only commandKind `internal.release.auto_approval` under principal `daemon:release-auto-approval` (precedent `internal.release.receipt` / `daemon:release`, release-receipt-contracts.ts:24-26) on its OWN aggregate `release-auto:<goalId>` so evaluating never bumps `release:<goalId>` and never invalidates a human's offered expectedVersion; keyed by the deterministic commandId from step 4; exact keys `{version: "moe-release-auto-approval/1", commandId, goalId, sha, optIn: {action, tier}, sliceRef, subjectTier, reasonCodes}`; `readReleaseAutoApproval(store, projectId, commandId)`. NOT a runtime kind — an arm asserts it is absent from RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS so no digest mirror rotates. NEVER declare a `*_LAYER`/`*_LAYERS` constant in either new module: the security scanners register it and demand a roster backfill. RED ARMS FIRST (in the step-7 test file): R0 subject + opt-in `{action: "release.decide", tier: "R1"}` -> ALLOW naming that opt-in; R2 and R3 subjects -> yield carrying HUMAN_ONLY_TIER; a slice whose only opt-in is for "preview.decide" -> AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN (exact action match, policy-evaluation.ts:157); two installed evaluation slices with the NEWEST lacking the opt-in -> not opted in (foldSlices takes the LAST slice's optIns, policy-composition.ts:161-166).
implementationPlan.note:
THE LEAF LANDED, SPLIT IN TWO. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --config package.json --maxWorkers=1 --testTimeout=60000 src/release/release-auto-decide.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 14 passed (14)`. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` EXIT 0.

DEVIATION 1 — TWO MODULES, NOT ONE. The step names one module holding both the evaluation and the record codec+ledger. Written as one it measured ~460 lines, well over the 250 target and heading for the 400 hard cap, so it is split on the seam Gate 2 split on: `release-auto-approval.ts` (233) is the decision, `release-auto-approval-record.ts` (230) is the durable record. Both under 250. This makes the row's path roster 11 rather than 9; the per-FILE cap is the binding rail and splitting is the sanctioned fix, so I took it rather than shipping one over-target file.

DEVIATION 2 — `evaluateReleaseAutoApproval(store, {decidedAt, goalId, operatorPrincipalId, projectId})`, not the step's `{projectId, goalId, sha, operatorPrincipalId}`. The evaluation does not read `sha` at all, so carrying it would have been an unused parameter; `sha` lives on the RECORD input where it is actually used. `decidedAt` replaces it because `evaluatedAtEpochMs` is a required engine operand and must be bound server-side, exactly as Gate 2 does.

DEVIATION 3 — SELECTION IS "NEWEST INSTALLED EVALUATION SLICE", not Gate 2's "the one slice declaring this opt-in". Deliberate and stricter: an operator installing a fresh policy with no opt-in has turned automatic release OFF. The step's own last-slice-wins red arm demands this reading, and it is armed.

CODE ROSTER: RELEASE_AUTO_CODE_LAYER_MAP with six keys over two surfaces — NOT_ALLOWED and POLICY_INPUT_INVALID at "CORE_REDUCER" (the same literal Gate 2 uses), and OPT_IN_UNNAMEABLE / POLICY_UNRESOLVED / TIER_UNCOVERED / TIER_UNRESOLVED at "RELEASE_AUTO_DECISION". The `_MAP` tail is the local convention release-decide-contracts.ts documents: both security scanners key on a name ending LAYER/LAYERS/BOUNDARIES immediately before the `=`, so this declares no rostered boundary. An arm greps BOTH new modules with the scanners' own pattern and asserts zero matches — that is what keeps this row from repeating the Gate 2 defect I filed as task-89300aa0557e430888d43f652165bf41.

THE 14 ARMS. R1 subject + R1 opt-in -> ALLOW naming `{action: "release.decide", tier: "R1"}` and the selected sliceRef; R1 subject + R0-capped release opt-in -> AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN @ CORE_REDUCER; opt-in for preview.decide only -> same (exact action match); newest slice drops the opt-in after an older one carried it -> same, with a positive control asserting it DID approve before the reset; stock journey (both seeded slices carry `autoApprovalOptIns: []`) -> same; R2 and R3 subjects -> HUMAN_ONLY_TIER @ CORE_REDUCER; POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS deep-equals ["R0","R1"]; roster derived from the map's keys with both surfaces present; the layer-scanner grep; record written on `release-auto:<goalId>` with `release:<goalId>`'s version PROVEN UNCHANGED; replay of the same commandId leaves the version unchanged; decoder refuses an extra key, an unknown tier, an unknown reason code, an extra opt-in key and a /2 version; and `internal.release.auto_approval` asserted ABSENT from RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.

FIXTURE FACT worth carrying: the R2/R3 arms RAISE the tier through the installed slice's own `riskClassifications` on the fact id this module composes (`release.run_policy_tier:run-1`), because the journey's run-policy row is fixed at R1 and a second row on that aggregate would read AMBIGUOUS. That is the operator-facing mechanism and the same fold `assessRisk` applies, so no tier is spelled into an arm.

implementationPlan.description: PROVENANCE ON THE RELEASE RECEIPT (DoD 2), three files. release-receipt-contracts.ts (165): bump RELEASE_RECEIPT_VERSION to `moe-release-receipt/2`, add the provenance key from step 1(2) to RECEIPT_KEYS (:46-49), and make the decoder (:127-165) admit BOTH vintages: version /1 with exactly the 9 old keys -> provenance null; /2 with exactly 10 keys, provenance null or `{action: non-empty string, tier in POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS}`; 11 keys or a tier outside the roster -> refused. THE HAZARD UNIQUE TO THIS ROW: `releaseReceiptId` (:106-108) HASHES RELEASE_RECEIPT_VERSION into the id. A naive bump rotates every receipt id: deploy-command.ts:297 and goal-deployment-read.ts:46 recompute the new id and lose every stored /1 RELEASED receipt, and decode's `receiptId !== releaseReceiptId(...)` check at :148 turns stored /1 receipts RELEASE_RECEIPT_INVALID, which release-evidence-read.ts:180-186 escalates to UNREADABLE for the whole release read. Pin `RECEIPT_ID_DOMAIN = "moe-release-receipt/1"` as a separate literal used ONLY in the id hash; an arm asserts a /2 receipt's id equals sha256 over the literal-domain tuple and that a /1 receipt written before the bump still resolves by id. release-receipt-ledger.ts (155): `RecordReleaseReceiptInput` (:47-56) gains `provenance`; the write path passes it through; readers unchanged. release-decide-service.ts (227 -> ~240, near the 250 target; if over, move the join into the ledger by passing commandId): `record()` (:127-142) joins `readReleaseAutoApproval(store, projectId, envelope.commandId)` and sets `provenance = rec !== null && rec.goalId === goalId && rec.sha === sha ? rec.optIn : null`. A human dispatch (random UUID commandId, composition :424) finds no record -> null. The wrapper's 3-key terminal, DurableDecision, and the payload roster `["base","decision","goalId","sha"]` (payload-keys.ts:177) are UNTOUCHED — the wire contract does not move. release-evidence-read.ts's projection (:67-75) withholds fields by design; leave it (a card-visible provenance is a follow-up comment, not this row). RED ARMS (step-7 file): /1 bytes decode with provenance null; /2 with provenance decodes with the VALUES; /2 with 11 keys refused; /2 with tier "R2" refused; id stability across the bump; service: human dispatch -> null, auto record present -> `{action, tier}` values.
implementationPlan.note:
PROVENANCE ON THE RELEASE RECEIPT, WITHOUT A VERSION BUMP. Full deviation record with the measurement on comment-0f38dfa3. Headline: the step says bump to `moe-release-receipt/2`; release-receipt-ledger.test.ts:56 pins a freshly written receipt to /1 and the same plan's step 7 requires that file to stay at 8 untouched, so the two instructions are mutually unsatisfiable. Shipped `provenance` as an OPTIONAL key at the UNCHANGED version, which satisfies DoD 2 (the record NAMES action and tier), keeps the foreign file green and untouched, and retires the receipt-id rotation hazard entirely rather than pinning around it.

FILES. release-receipt-contracts.ts 165 -> 239: new `ReleaseReceiptProvenance {action, tier: PolicyAutoApprovalTier}` (narrower than the engine's four tiers on purpose), `provenance` on `ReleaseReceiptV1` as TOTAL in memory / OPTIONAL on the wire, `exact()` now admits exactly the nine required keys optionally plus `provenance` and nothing else, and `persistedProvenance` keeps "absent" (a human) apart from "malformed" (a refusal). release-receipt-ledger.ts 155 -> 170: optional `provenance` on the input; the write OMITS the key when null so a human release writes byte-identical bytes and a replay stays a replay. release-decide-service.ts 227 -> 237: reads `readReleaseAutoApproval(store, projectId, envelope.commandId)` ONCE before any write and re-checks it against (goalId, sha); a human dispatch carries a random uuid, finds nothing, records null.

ALSO TIGHTENED, from the typechecker: `ReleaseAutoOptIn.tier` is now `PolicyAutoApprovalTier` and both `nameableOptIn` and `persistedOptIn` select from POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS. A durable slice is JSON and could carry an R2 ceiling; that is not an auto-approval declaration, so it is now UNNAMEABLE and the gate declines instead of recording provenance the operator never expressed. Strictly fail-closed.

ARMS ADDED (8 more in the new file, 22 total there): 9-key body decodes with provenance null and is asserted to BE nine keys; a body with provenance decodes with the VALUES; eight forged shapes each labelled and each asserted to carry RELEASE_RECEIPT_INVALID (tier R2, tier R9, empty action, extra key inside provenance, missing key inside provenance, explicit null, provenance plus a foreign extra key, and a foreign extra key alone); the id derivation pinned to the string literal `"moe-release-receipt/1"` with provenance-independence proven; a human write proven to omit the key from the STORED bytes; an automatic write proven to carry it through the ledger and back.

implementationPlan.description: THE RECONCILER: apps/daemon/src/release/release-auto-decide.ts (NEW, target <=250) plus its `.js` bridge. WHY NOT GATE 2's SHAPE: Gate 2 fires from preview.start's async completion. Gate 3 has NO in-daemon completion moment — criterion receipts (criterion-runner.ts:104-111) and PUSHED publish receipts (publish-ledger.ts:180) are written by the WRAPPER's delivery.advance() (agent-wrapper-main.ts:316,:350), the dossier is recorded lazily INSIDE a release.decide dispatch (release-production-wiring.ts:62-71), and no store reactor exists. So: `registerReleaseAutoDecide(schedules, deps)` registers job id `"release/auto-decide"` on the EXISTING DurableSchedule (durable-schedule.ts:88 register; single-flight per job built in at :66; interval DEFAULT_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_MS 60_000). Per tick: `readPublishLedger(store, projectId)` -> per goal `readRunGoalPublication(...)` (run-goal-publication.ts:7-22) -> candidates with `outcome === "PUSHED"` and non-null sha. PER CANDIDATE, IN THIS ORDER, BEFORE ANY JOURNAL WRITE — order is load-bearing, see attack A10: (0) `commandId = sha256hex(JSON.stringify(["release-auto", projectId, goalId, sha]))`; `store.getCommandDecision({commandId, principalId: operatorPrincipalId, projectId}) !== null` -> SKIP ALREADY_ATTEMPTED (ONE automatic attempt per (goal, sha); a REFUSED auto terminal parks the sha for a human — a documented bound, because a retried deterministic id hits RELEASE_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT once the version moved). (1) `readReleaseReceipt(store, projectId, releaseReceiptId(projectId, goalId, sha, "RELEASED", null)).ok` -> yield `RELEASE_COMMAND_ID_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM` (the service's own pair, :186). (2) HUMAN REJECT WINS (DoD 5): walk `store.readEvents(releaseDossierAggregateId(goalId))`; any `ReleaseCommandDecided` whose payload decodes to `{outcome: "DECIDED", resultCode: "REJECTED", effectId: null}` (release-decide-command.ts:213-217) -> yield `RELEASE_COMMAND_ID_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_COMMAND_SEAM` with detail naming `event.decisionTrace.principalId`. Scope is PER GOAL: any recorded REJECT parks the goal's automatic path until a human decides; a new sha does not un-park it. The auto path never REJECTs, so REJECTED == human by construction; the service is NOT made sticky for a later human APPROVE. (3) an Admitted without a Decided on the same walk (hasPendingRelease, :113-125) -> SKIP. (4) `dossierFacts(goalId, sha)` null -> SKIP; `releaseDossierGaps(facts.input, sha, facts.ancestry)` non-empty -> yield `RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` carrying `gaps[].code` (DoD 3 asserts the CODE from this yield — the service's own detail names only criterion ids). NO dispatch on gaps. (5) step-2 policy not ALLOW -> yield `{code: reasonCodes, layer: <step 1(2) literal>}`. (6) write the auto-approval record. (7) `expectedVersion = store.getAggregateVersion(releaseDossierAggregateId(goalId))` — read AFTER the walk. (8) dispatch through `registry.get(RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND)?.asyncHandler` on the ALREADY-COMPOSED registry (never a second createAsyncCommandEntries — that mints a second PR port; async-entries.ts:174-181 forbids a second push path), with a synthesized envelope that survives decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes (release-decide-command.ts:94): exact keys `commandId, commandKind: "release.decide", correlationId, expectedVersion, payload: {base, decision: "APPROVE", goalId, sha}, requestDigest` (sha256 of the payload bytes; the wrapper recomputes identity from the server-known principal, :169-175), `schemaVersion: RUNTIME_COMMAND_ENVELOPE_VERSION, sessionCredential: "daemon:release-auto-decide"` (never authenticated on this path; document that this is the boot-reconciliation precedent, not a hole), `targetAggregateId: releaseDossierAggregateId(goalId)`.
